acceptance: agent-write-preflight (or worktree lifecycle metadata) records the owning session and refuses or warns when a second live session writes in the same worktree
A test shows a second claimant is refused or warned, and the owner can release or transfer the worktree
context: agent-write-preflight pins identity and location but not an owner. The conflict was found by seeing an unexpected commit appear in the branch log and a second agent process running tests in the same directory. Related guard: worktree lifecycle metadata already exists for each worktree.
description: Two sessions worked in the same linked worktrees for pull requests 3548 and 3549 at once. One session committed to the other's branch, ran a baseline rewrite in the worktree while the first was publishing, and a pre-push hook run failed because uncommitted edits from the other session made it modify files and stash-restore conflict. Nothing records or checks which session owns a worktree, so competing edits only show up as odd commits or failed pushes.
